title: Internal transfer: velocity template + role symmetry guide
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a lightweight, repeatable template for handling internal candidate moves (lateral and upward) with speed and low friction. Focus is on: clear manager coordination, bias-aware rubrics that respect existing performance signals, a short offer timeline, and a compact handoff checklist so the individual can start contributing in-week. Not intended to replace full external hiring playbooks; this is the fast path for internal mobility.

When to use this: quick transfers where candidate is internal and has >=3 months in current role OR has an explicit manager nomination. Use instead of full-blind hire flow when risk tolerance is medium/low and manager alignment exists. If candidate requests relocation or compensation uplift >15%, escalate to compensation review.

High-level timeline (target):
- Day 0 (nomination) — hiring manager files the ‘internal move request’ (JIRA-HR-6789) and alerts current manager + People Ops.
- Day 1 — quick sync between people ops, hiring manager, and current manager (15–30m). Confirm role scope, expected impact, compensation guardrails, and overlap window.
- Day 2–4 — compact assessment (1–2 conversations + work sample if needed). Use role-symmetry rubric below.
- Day 5 — final manager calibration, verbal offer.
- Day 7 — written offer & proposed start date.
- Start date to +14 days — handoff period and buddy pairing.

Minimum checks (people ops):
- Verify eligibility (probation, performance flags, active PIP? flag and pause).
- Confirm manager-to-manager alignment on scope and timing.
- Preliminary comp band check; if outside band, open comp review ASAP.
- Security and access implications flagged for infra/data roles; route to security.

Role-symmetry rubric (compact, bias-resistant):
- Core criteria (use short anchors: scope, impact, craft, autonomy, collaboration). For each criterion use: Evidence (examples), Gap (red/amber/green), Decision weight (0.2–0.4). Keep to 5 rows.
- Example anchors:
  - Scope: breadth of ownership (green = leads cross-team initiative; amber = owns major component; red = contributor only).
  - Impact: measurable outcomes (green = drove product metric improvement; amber = regular deliverables; red = limited product tie).
  - Craft: skill match to role (green = direct experience; amber = transferrable; red = heavy training needed).
  - Autonomy: works with minimal ramp; capacity to run projects.
  - Collaboration / stakeholder mgmt: evidence of cross-functional influence.
- Weight example: Scope 0.25, Impact 0.25, Craft 0.25, Autonomy 0.15, Collaboration 0.10. Use manager discretion but document numeric scores.

Interview choreography (if assessment needed):
- Keep number of touchpoints <=2. Typical pattern: 1x role manager deep-dive (30m) + 1x cross-functional partner (20m) OR 1x takehome micro-task (max 3 hours) + 1x manager sync.
- Avoid long whiteboard tests for internal candidates; prefer context-based conversation ("describe a time you shipped X within constraints Y").
- For engineers: if code sample used, make it domain-relevant and time-boxed (no more than 3 hours).
- Interviewers must explicitly reference prior internal performance signals (reviews, project history) and document how those signals influenced rating.

Compensation and leveling guide (quick rules):
- Standard internal uplift cap: +10% without VP approval. Anything >10% requires people ops + comp committee review.
- Promotions that change level require a short promotion justification memo (one paragraph) and manager concurrence.
- If the role is funded in a different team with higher band, check budget owners for reallocation.

Offer & acceptance practicals:
- Verbal offer window target: within 5 business days of nomination.
- Written offer available within 48 hours of verbal acceptance.
- If current manager requests a counteroffer discussion, people ops mediates but ensure timeline stays short (max 2 business days).

Handoff checklist (pre-start & first 14 days):
Pre-start (to be completed before public announcement):
- Agree start date and overlaps; confirm owner of ongoing projects.
- Document TO-DOs: code ownership handoff, ticket owners re-assigned, runbook updates, pager rotation changes.
- Prepare buddy assignment and 1-week intro agenda.
- Update org chart + access provisioning requests queued.

First 7 days (integration sprint):
- Day 1: intro with new team, role expectations doc, immediate first ticket scoped.
- Day 2–3: paired work with buddy on a live task; 30m daily sync with manager.
- Day 4–7: small independent deliverable due; manager gives feedback in writing.

Days 8–14:
- Stakeholder ramp: 1:1s with two cross-functional partners scheduled.
- Checkpoint: manager writes 14-day note summarizing progress & outstanding risks.

Mentoring & success signals:
- Assign a mentor (not the manager) for first 30 days: weekly 30m check-ins.
- Success at 30 days: shipping first small deliverable and two positive stakeholder refs.
- Success markers at 90 days: full role responsibilities taken, measurable contribution to team metric.

Risk mitigations & edge cases: 
- Active PIP or open performance concerns: pause the move until documented improvement; exception requires people ops + HR lead sign-off.
- Dual reporting scenarios: if candidate will straddle teams for >2 weeks, create explicit SLA for conflict resolution and time allocation.
- Critical project coverage: if move would create a coverage gap on a high-priority project, include a contingency plan for 2–4 week coverage and a named temporary owner.

Manager checklist (quick-to-follow):
- Before nomination: 15m alignment w/ current manager + read latest performance snapshot.
- During assessment: focus on evidence and reduce hypothetical questions.
- On offer: prepare transition plan and public announcement draft.
- After start: daily nudges first week, weekly written checkpoint first month.

Notes to people ops (process ops):
- Keep the flow asynchronous where possible: use JIRA for approvals, Slack threads for quick alignment.
- Track time to hire for internal moves separately from external hires; target median = 7 days.
- Collect anonymized feedback from candidate & both managers at 14d and 90d to tune the template.

Appendix (templates):
- One-paragraph promotion justification (template): '[Name] is being elevated to [level] because [two-sentence evidence]. Expected impact: [measure]. Manager sign-off: [name].'
- 14-day manager checkpoint template (bullet): wins, blockers, risk level, plan.
- Public announcement script (short): 'Join me in congratulating [Name] who will start as [role] on [date]. They will be owned by [manager] and continue a temporary overlap with [old manager] until [date].'

Open questions / follow-ups (things to resolve in next iteration):
- Should we allow an expedited 48-hour path for senior IC transfers when cross-team priority is >90%?
- How do we incorporate cross-region moves (visa/tax implications) into the 7-day target?
- Metrics to track: time-to-internal-offer, % internal offers accepted, post-move retention at 6 months.

Quick wins to roll out this month:
- Pilot with two hiring managers in Eng + Product and target median TTM (time-to-move) <= 7 days.
- Automate pre-start checklist using a simple Google Form that populates a JIRA checklist.

(Informal notes)
- This doc intentionally short, keep it simple for managers. Will iterate after pilot.
- Reuse existing fields in performance system where possible to avoid duplicative evidence gathering.

END
